title: Why Loops
goal: In this lesson you will learn why programs need repetition, and how copying the same line many times is a clue that a loop would help.
learn: Repetition means doing the same idea again
Copy-paste code gets long and hard to change
Loops exist so one block can run many times
idea: Sometimes a program must do the same kind of step again and again. Print five stars, count to ten, or greet every player. You could copy the same line many times. That works for a tiny example, but it is slow to write and easy to mess up when you change one number. A loop is Python’s way to say: “run this block more than once.” Later lessons teach for and while. Today, notice the problem loops solve.

lines: # Changing "five" to "twenty" would mean many edits

changeOneLine: In the editor above, change the last line from Done printing stars to Stars finished. Press Run. Only the last line of output should change.

lines: # Clue: the same print runs three times

practice.text: Finish a cheer that prints Go! three times, then prints Yay!. Use separate print lines (no loop yet).
practice.hint: You already have one Go!. Fill the two empty print() lines so Go! shows three times in a row before Yay!.
practice.starterTip: Try print("Go!") in both blank lines. Then Run and check you see three Go! lines, then Yay!.
practice.starter:
# Cheer three times
print("Go!")
print()
print()
print("Yay!")
practice.gradingNote: Pass if Go! appears three times and Yay! appears once after them. Empty print() fails.

practice.text: Print the word Step four times on four lines. Fill in the blanks.
practice.hint: Each empty print() should show the same word as the first line. Step inside quotes.
practice.starterTip: Copy the idea from line 1: put print("Step") inside each of the three blank print() calls.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if Step prints on exactly four lines (four non-empty prints).

quiz.question: Why might repeating the same print() line ten times be a problem?

options.text: Python only allows two print() calls
It is long to write and hard to change later
print() cannot show the same text twice
Comments are not allowed near print()

quiz.correct: Copy-paste works for tiny demos but gets messy when you need many repeats.
quiz.wrong: Think about editing: changing ten copied lines is slower than changing one loop.

quiz.question: What is a loop for?

options.text: To store a single number only
To run a block of code more than once

quiz.correct: A loop repeats a block so you do not copy the same lines by hand.
quiz.wrong: Loops exist so one indented block can run many times.

quiz.question: If you see the same print written five times in a row, what is that a clue for?

options.text: A loop might be a better fit

quiz.correct: Repeated lines are a signal that a loop could shorten the program.
quiz.wrong: Same-step-over-and-over is exactly what loops are designed for.

project.title: Five High Fives
project.desc: Without using a loop yet, print High five! on five lines, then print Team win! once at the end.
project.starter:
# Five cheers
print("High five!")
